meta.title: SudoCut
meta.description: Upload the raw footage, get a cut back. We remove the silence, the filler, the retakes and the tangents.

home.intro: Four hours of footage. One story. Ninety seconds of work.
home.body: SudoCut finds the silence, the filler, the retakes and the tangents in your footage. It proposes the cuts. You make the call.

about.title: SudoCut builds one thing.
about.lede: An editor that removes what nobody watches. That's the whole company.

body.one: It does the pass an editor does by hand: strip the silence, cut the stumbles, drop the tangents. What's left is the part that needs a human.
body.two: Korean is the default. English runs in parallel. Neither is a translation of the other — both are written in their own language.
body.three: Every cut carries its reason on screen: silence, filler, retake, tangent, needs review. Nothing disappears without one.

principles.title: What we hold to
principles.two: Numbers instead of adjectives. 6:12, not "significant time savings."
principles.three: Editor to editor. We don't explain what you already know.
principles.four: Honesty over polish. The failures get written down too.

body.one: SudoCut is small and builds one thing. There is no roster on this page — not as mystique. We just haven't published one.
body.two: The rest of this page is how the work actually gets decided. On most team pages that part is filler around the photos. Here it is the part we can source.

empty.label: Not published
empty.body: Names, roles and one line each go in this grid. It is empty because nothing has been cleared for publication yet. The team exists; the list doesn't.

principles.title: How the work gets decided
principles.one: We are not artists. An artist spreads across everything. We go narrow, on purpose.
principles.two: Direction over perfection. Decide, ship it, iterate. It can change later.
principles.three: Honesty over polish. The failures and the dead ends get written down with everything else.
principles.four: AI proposes; humans decide. Automating until nobody can step in is worse, not better.

pricing.title: The beta is free. Launch won't be.
pricing.lede: Both cards are below, including the one that isn't switched on yet.

body.one: Beta channels get access free, plus a one-time grant of 600 raw minutes. There is no subscription charge during the beta. The only payment that exists is a one-time credit top-up — no card on file, nothing that renews.
body.two: The launch card is a target, not a live price. We publish it now because a channel deserves to know what launch costs before it moves a workflow onto us. None of it can be bought today; billing isn't built.
